# kbo

Belgian enterprise (KBO Open Data) lookup: API and web UI.

- **Production:** https://kbo.co-creative.be; resource group `rg-kbo` (web app `kbo-web`, job `kbo-build`).
- **Platform definition:** `apps/kbo/main.bicepparam` in `co-creative/platform`.

## What this is

A .NET 11 solution for the Belgian **KBO open data** (Kruispuntbank van Ondernemingen, the crossroads bank for enterprises): look up and search all ~2M Belgian enterprises.

**Rewrite in progress.** Read `specs/azure-architecture.md` first. Each monthly KBO "Full" zip becomes **one immutable, read-only SQLite file** (`kbo-<extract>.db`) built by a Container Apps job. A single scale-to-zero web app (minimal API + static-SSR Blazor UI) reads that file directly from an Azure Files share. There's no incremental import and no database server.

- **Done:** phase 1 (the core library and the build tool), phase 2 (the web app) and phase 3 (Azure: the `kbo-build` job and the `kbo-web` app are live).
- **Next:** phase 4 (deleting the legacy projects).

The official data-model description is `Net.Code.Kbo.Data/Cookbook-KBO-Open-Data.pdf`. The data isn't in the repo: download it from kbopub.economie.fgov.be after creating an account.

## Solution layout

| Project | Role |
|---|---|
| `Net.Code.Kbo` | Core library: `KboNr`/`EntityNumber`, the company document model (`Documents.cs`, JSON source-generated via `KboJson`), `CodeBook`, `SearchQuery` (input → FTS5 MATCH), `CompanyStore` (read-only queries on a release db). |
| `Net.Code.Kbo.Build` | Console tool, assembly `kbo`: `build`, `release` (the job), `get`, `search`. Turns a KBO zip into a release db. |
| `Net.Code.Kbo.Web` | The web app: JSON API under `/api` (`CompanyApi.cs`) plus a Blazor UI with **static SSR only** (no interactive render modes), both using `CompanyStore` in-process. `ReleaseProvider` opens `Kbo:Database` (a .db path, used in dev and tests) or `Kbo:Share` (a directory with `current.txt`, used in Azure). |
| `Net.Code.Kbo.Tests` | TUnit tests for the projects above: fixture zip (`KboFixture`), plus web tests through `WebApplicationFactory` (`WebApp`). |
| `kbo.AppHost`, `kbo.ServiceDefaults` | Aspire: the AppHost runs `Net.Code.Kbo.Web`; phase 3 adds the Azure resources. |
| `specs/azure-architecture.md` | **The plan**: decisions, schema, document shape, release flow, API/UI design, measurements, open questions. |
| *Legacy, deleted in phase 4:* `Net.Code.Kbo.Data`, `Net.Code.Kbo.Cli`, `Net.Code.Kbo.Api`, `Net.Code.Kbo.Data.Tests`, the other `specs/*` | The EF Core / incremental-import implementation. **Don't extend it.** |

## Build, run, test

```sh
dotnet build kbo.sln
dotnet test                                     # all test projects (global.json opts into Microsoft.Testing.Platform)
dotnet run --project Net.Code.Kbo.Tests         # new tests only
dotnet run --project Net.Code.Kbo.Tests -- --treenode-filter "/*/*/SearchQueryTests/*"

# release database from a KBO Full zip (about 7.5 min and 3.2 GB RAM for the real extract)
dotnet run -c Release --project Net.Code.Kbo.Build -- build -i KboOpenData_0502_..._Full.zip -o data/kbo-0502.db
dotnet run -c Release --project Net.Code.Kbo.Build -- search -d data/kbo-0502.db colruyt halle
dotnet run -c Release --project Net.Code.Kbo.Build -- get -d data/kbo-0502.db 0403.170.701
dotnet run -c Release --project Net.Code.Kbo.Build -- release --share <dir> [--work <dir>]

# web app on http://localhost:5280, serving ../data/kbo-0502.db (appsettings.Development.json)
dotnet run --project Net.Code.Kbo.Web            # or: dotnet run --project kbo.AppHost
```

- `data/` is gitignored. Never commit `.db` files or KBO data.
- TUnit assertions are async: `await Assert.That(x).IsEqualTo(y);`.
- `KboFixture` is a tiny KBO-shaped zip with the edge cases that matter: units, quoted names with commas and doubled quotes, a struck-off address, a FAX contact, several NACE versions, an orphan row. When you change parsing, the document shape or search, extend it and `ReleaseBuilderTests`.
- `BuiltRelease` opens its store with `commonTermFraction: 0.5`. In a 4-company fixture, the 10% default would treat every word as common.
- Web tests use `WebApplicationFactory<Net.Code.Kbo.Web.Components.App>`. `Program` can't be the marker, because the `kbo` tool also has a top-level `Program` and the test project sees both.
- For performance-sensitive changes, build the real zip and compare against the measurements in §11 of the plan.

## Key design points (details in the plan)

- **Build (`ExtractModel`):** loads the whole extract into memory (about 3.2 GB), streaming CSVs straight from the zip with Net.Code.Csv. It then writes one row per enterprise, in number order, to `company` (summary + document JSON) and `company_fts`. Establishments and branches are nested in their enterprise's document.
- **Documents:** they store codes, not descriptions; `CodeBook` resolves descriptions per language (falling back to NL, then FR, then any language). Empty values are omitted from the JSON.
- **Activities:** a document keeps only the newest NACE version per (activity group, classification). The search index holds the descriptions of all versions.
- **Skipped or kept data:**
  - Struck-off addresses stay in the document with `strikingOff`, but aren't searchable.
  - FAX contacts are skipped, because `code.csv` has no FAX code.
  - Orphan rows are counted (`orphanEntities`).
- **Search index:** `company_fts` is contentless and its rowid is the enterprise number. It has **no prefix index**, a deliberate choice: one would add 1.8 GB. `company_fts_vocab` (fts5vocab) gives per-word document counts.
- **Search queries (`CompanyStore.Search`):**
  - Sort and limit inside the FTS subquery, then join `company`; joining first is 3–4× slower.
  - Free-text words matching more than 10% of companies are dropped. If nothing else remains, results come back unranked.
- **Opening a release:** `CompanyStore` opens the file as `file:<path>?immutable=1` read-only, with one pooled connection per call. A published release file must never change in place.
- **Releasing (`Releaser`):** takes the newest `incoming/*_Full.zip` newer than `current.txt`, builds and validates it, copies it to the share, and writes `current.txt` last. It keeps the current and previous release and moves the zip to `incoming/processed/`. Validation errors mean nothing is published (exit code 1).

## Web app notes

- **No release yet:** the app starts without one (platform contract: `/health` answers 200 with no data). `ReleaseProvider.Current` is then null and opening is retried on demand, at most every `Kbo:RetryInterval` (10 s). Meanwhile the API returns 503 problem details (`NoReleaseException`) and `MainLayout` shows "No data yet" instead of the page. Once a release is open, `current.txt` is checked again on demand, at most every `Kbo:CheckInterval` (1 min). When it names another file (a new release or a rollback), that file is opened and swapped in; if it can't be opened, the open release is kept.

- **Language:** `?lang=nl|fr` in the query string; anything else falls back to nl. `code.csv` only has NL and FR descriptions. `CompanyView`/`SummaryView` (`Net.Code.Kbo/Views.cs`) resolve codes for both the API and the UI.
- **Not found:**
  - Pages call `NavigationManager.NotFound()`, which renders `Pages/NotFound.razor` with status 404.
  - Unknown non-API URLs are re-executed to `/not-found`. This needs the explicit `UseRouting()` after the status-code middleware in `Program.cs`.
  - API errors are problem details.
  - Don't set `Response.StatusCode` by hand in components: the body comes out empty.
- **Encoding:** HTML is written with all Unicode ranges allowed (`AddWebEncoders`), so accented names aren't turned into `&#xE9;`.
- **Caching:** API responses carry `ETag: "<extract>-<builtAt>"` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`; `If-None-Match` gives 304.

## Conventions

- Target framework `net11.0` everywhere, with nullable and implicit usings. Microsoft packages are on `11.0.0-rc.*` until .NET 11 GA; bump them then.
- Prefer records, primary constructors, `switch` expressions and list patterns. Keep the code plain: simplicity is a stated priority.
- Commit directly on `main`.
- `specs/azure-architecture.md` is the source of truth for the design. Update it when you change a decision, and record measurements in §11.

# Delivery flow

Every co-creative repository picks its delivery flow in `.co-creative.yml` at the repository root. The repository
owns that file and changes it with an ordinary commit:

```yaml
delivery: push   # push | pr-auto | pr-review
```

No file, no `delivery` key or an unknown value means **`push`**. Read the file before your first commit in a session.

## Always, whatever the flow

- **Run the tests locally before every push** (`dotnet test`, or the repository's test command named in its
  README/AGENTS.md). Don't push while they fail; if a failure isn't yours, say so and stop.
- CI runs the tests again before anything deploys. A red CI run is yours to fix first.
- Conventional Commit messages; one logical change per commit.

## `push` (default)

1. Run the tests, then commit on the default branch (`main` or `master`).
2. Push. In an app repository every push to the default branch is a production delivery.
3. Watch the CI run (`gh run watch`, or `gh run list --limit 1`). If it fails, forward-fix with a new commit; don't
   rewrite pushed history.

## `pr-auto`

1. Create a branch (`<type>/<short-name>`, e.g. `fix/health-timeout`), run the tests, commit and push the branch.
2. `gh pr create --fill` (or with a short title and body: what, why, how you tested it).
3. Wait for the checks (`gh pr checks --watch`). Pull requests only run the tests; nothing deploys.
4. When they pass, `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`. That merge is the production delivery; watch its run as
   with `push`.
5. When a check fails, fix it on the branch and push again. Never merge a red PR.

## `pr-review`

As `pr-auto` up to and including step 3. Then **stop**: report the PR link and the check result, and leave the
merge to a person. Don't merge, even when the checks pass or someone asks another session to do it.

A direct push to the default branch in a `pr-*` repository isn't blocked (GitHub Free has no branch protection for
private repositories): CI deploys it and records a warning. Don't rely on that; follow the flow.

# co-creative app repository

This repository is an app on the **co-creative platform** (Azure Container Apps or Static Web Apps, one Azure
subscription, budget €10/month for the base platform). The platform itself lives in `co-creative/platform`.

## Non-negotiable rules

1. **No secrets, ever.** Never commit, log or print keys, connection strings, tokens or passwords. Azure access uses
   the app's managed identity (`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`; `ManagedIdentityCredential` in Azure, `DefaultAzureCredential`
   locally). If something seems to need a secret, stop and ask: the platform probably offers a keyless way.
2. **Respect the ownership split.** This repository owns its code, `platform.app.json` (settings, scale, schedules)
   and `infra/app.bicep` (its own storage, SQL, Service Bus, SignalR) and `.co-creative.yml` (its delivery flow).
   The platform owns which components exist, sign-in, hostnames, DNS, mounts, AI and the ceilings. Platform-owned
   files here (`platform.md`, `.github/workflows/platform-deploy.yml`, `.github/platform/*`) change only through
   `platform/sync` pull requests, which the platform merges itself: never edit them.
3. **`main` (or `master`) is production.** Every push deploys after the CI tests pass. Run the tests locally before
   every push and follow the repository's delivery flow (`.co-creative.yml`, default `push`; see the delivery
   rules). Changing `platform.app.json` or `infra/app.bicep` is a production change: say so before doing it.
4. **Keep the runtime contract** (see `platform.md`): one Dockerfile target per component, no command/args
   overrides. The **web** component serves HTTP on port 8080 and `GET /health` returns 200 as soon as the process
   runs (also without data). **Jobs** have no port or health endpoint: they run once and exit, with exit code 0 for
   success; a non-zero exit marks the execution failed.
5. **Spec first for material changes.** New features, behaviour changes and architecture decisions go through the
   spec-driven workflow (`openspec/`), before code.

## Where to look

- `platform.md`: this app's platform contract, delivery steps and what the platform provides.
- Skill **co-creative-platform**: the platform model, ownership, delivery and how to work with the platform team.
- **Reusable packages:** the private co-creative NuGet feed (GitHub Packages) holds shared libraries such as the
  design system `CoCreative.UI`. Look there before building something reusable; publish code there when two or
  more apps need it (`CoCreative.*` names). See skill co-creative-platform, packages.
- Skill **co-creative-coding**: architecture and coding guidelines (C#/.NET, Blazor, tests).
- Skill **co-creative-specs**: the spec-driven workflow with OpenSpec.
- .NET skills (`csharp-expert`, `csharp-refactoring`, `dotnet-webapi`, Blazor, EF Core, testing, .NET 11) and Azure
  skills (`azure-*`): use them for their topics instead of guessing APIs.
- MCP servers: **microsoft-learn** for Microsoft and Azure documentation (verify APIs and limits there; don't rely on
  memory for SDK signatures), **azure** for read-only inspection of Azure resources.

## Working style

- Small, reviewable changes; run `dotnet test` (or the repository's test command) before declaring work done.
- Report outcomes faithfully: say what you verified and what you didn't.
- Use Conventional Commit prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `test:`).
